Subject: Post-call: Billing & procurement pathways / PO vs card for Redwood pilot

Thanks again for taking the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps on procurement readiness so we can scope the pilot without surprises. Notes below from our end: 

- Goal: 3-week pilot (non-production) for R&D team, expected spend ~ $6k–$12k depending on usage pattern.
- Key procurement questions we need to confirm:
  - Preferred payment vehicle: PO (net-30) vs corporate card?
  - Vendor onboarding: W-9, insurance cert, bank/ACH details, and whether a vendor form is required.
  - Marketplace: do you prefer procurement via AWS Marketplace (saves PO) or direct invoicing to your AP team?

Ask: Can you confirm which path (PO vs card vs marketplace) is workable for a pilot in July and who the procurement contact is? If PO is required, what is the typical approval lead time?

Attached: Redwood_Onboarding_Guide.pdf — includes sample SOW/term summary and our standard smaller-engagement billing options.

If easier, we can do a short 15-min sync with your procurement contact next week to unblock.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Post-call: Billing & procurement pathways / PO vs card for Redwood pilot

Thanks for the clear recap, Sergio. Good call. Quick answers from procurement/finance POV: 

- Card vs PO: Our AP policy generally prefers PO for any vendor spend > $10k per month. For one-off pilots under $5k, card is easiest (via corporate card). Between $5k–$10k we often need sponsor approval that can add a week.
- Vendor onboarding: We require a filled vendor profile (Procurement Form), W-9, standard vendor insurance (general liability), and ACH instructions.
- Marketplace: We do use AWS Marketplace for several SaaS vendors. Procurement likes marketplace for recurring software because it avoids manual PO processing, but it introduces our account team to Marketplace billing cycles. For a pilot, marketplace is acceptable if Redwood is listed and the pilot terms match (metered or monthly subscription).

Procurement contact: Priya Malhotra (pri.malhotra@acebiotech.com) — she handles vendor setup and will triage what we need for the vendor profile. Tom is our engineering sponsor and will own usage.

Attachments: I’m attaching our AP policy excerpt that shows the thresholds (AceBiotech_AP_Policies.pdf).

Next step: Can you send a one-page cost estimate for the pilot + a procurement checklist we can pass to Priya? If we can keep the pilot < $8k and provide the standard documents, I expect we can get a PO issued in ~7 business days.

— Jenna

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Billing & procurement pathways / PO vs card for Redwood pilot

Great — thanks Jenna and Tom, and hi Priya.

Priya, welcome — copying Karthik from our side to confirm technical onboarding items. Per Jenna’s note, here are two clean options so you can pick what fits Ace Biotech’s process: 

Option A — Marketplace (fastest) - We can provision the pilot through AWS Marketplace as a one-month usage agreement. Benefits: no PO required, immediate access, and Marketplace invoice to your AWS account. Limitation: Marketplace billing cadence is monthly and fees are billed through AWS.

Option B — Direct PO / Net-30 - We’ll provide a short purchase order-ready invoice and vendor profile docs (W-9 + insurance + ACH). We can accept a PO and invoice net-30. Typical PO processing for new vendors is ~7–10 business days on your side.

Suggested pilot structure to stay under the PO threshold: 3-week pilot with a capped usage not-to-exceed $8,000. If you confirm a cap, we’ll set usage alerts and cap enforcement to prevent billing surprises.

Attachments: Procurement_NextSteps_Checklist.docx (one-page vendor profile + docs list). Also included earlier: Redwood_Onboarding_Guide.pdf.

Action items:
- Priya: can you confirm which path you prefer (Marketplace vs PO) and whether Ace Biotech needs a vendor portal link filled?
- Tom: confirm the expected weekly spend estimate so we can set the cap in our dashboard.
- Karthik: if you could confirm the minimal technical details Priya will need (SLA, contact for support during pilot), that’d be great.

I’m available for a quick 15-min vendor-ops call Wed or Thu morning PT if that helps move this along faster.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
